import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/iris.csv')

# Create a scatter plot using seaborn
# Petal length and petal width are often the most discriminative features for Iris species
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 7))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='petal_length',
    y='petal_width',
    hue='species', # Differentiate species by color
    s=100, # Adjust marker size for better visibility
    alpha=0.8, # Add some transparency
    palette='viridis' # Choose a color palette
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Iris Petal Length vs. Petal Width by Species', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Petal Length (cm)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Petal Width (cm)', fontsize=12)

# Add a legend
plt.legend(title='Species', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Improve layout to prevent labels/legend from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/iris.csv')

# Create a scatter plot using seaborn
# Petal length and petal width are often the most discriminative features for Iris species
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 7))
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='petal_length',
    y='petal_width',
    hue='species', # Differentiate species by color
    s=100, # Adjust marker size for better visibility
    alpha=0.8, # Add some transparency
    palette='viridis' # Choose a color palette
)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Iris Petal Length vs. Petal Width by Species', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Petal Length (cm)', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Petal Width (cm)', fontsize=12)

# Add a legend
plt.legend(title='Species', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Improve layout to prevent labels/legend from being cut off
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
